rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has ‘say: reform for them’; Ṭāwūs instead reads ‘reform toward them.’
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (قل إصلاح لهم)، وعن طاووس إصلاح إليهم

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Ṭāwūs reads ‘reform toward them’ in place of the common reading ‘reform for them.’
rows.anchor: وعن طاووس إصلاح إليهم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading puts the final nūn of ‘your brothers’ in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة (فإخوانكم) برفع النون

rows.speaker: أبو مخلد
rows.claim: Abū Mikhlad reads ‘your brothers’ in the accusative, meaning ‘then mix with your brothers.’
rows.anchor: وعن أبي مخلد بالنصب على معنى تخالطوا إخوانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is one without a father; the term is used for children, with two cited verbal forms and patterns.
rows.anchor: اليتيم: من لا أب له، وإنما يطلق هذا الاسم على الأطفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mixing is combining two things so thoroughly that distinguishing them becomes difficult.
rows.anchor: وهو الجمع بين الشيئين بحيث يعسر تمييزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAnt is hardship and severity; to impose it is to burden someone unbearably, and it can mean sin because sin brings hardship.
rows.anchor: وأصل العنت المشقة والشدة، وأعنته: حمله على مشقة لا تطاق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes ‘clarifies’ as the governing verb for the circumstantial phrase ‘in this world and the next.’
rows.anchor: (يبين) في قول الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians take ‘they reflect’ as the governor of ‘in this world and the next.’
rows.anchor: و(يتفكرون) في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your brothers’ is nominative as a predicate: they remain your brothers whether or not you mix with them.
rows.anchor: رفع على معنى فهم إخوانكم خالطتموهم أو لم تخالطوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘On foot or riding’ is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, with an omitted verb meaning ‘pray.’
rows.anchor: وأما (رجالا) فتقديره: فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Arabs had treated orphans with great deference and strictness in the pre-Islamic period; after Islam they asked about their care, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك والسدي: كانت العرب في الجاهلية يعظمون شأن اليتيم

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع
rows.claim: After warnings against approaching orphans’ property and consuming it unjustly, people avoided all dealings and meals with orphans; their hardship and question occasioned the verse.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘they ask you’ refers to the people asking about orphans; an implicit element is needed because they did not ask about the orphans as persons and the answer is not about them as persons.
rows.anchor: الضمير في يسألونك قيل: يرجع إلى القوم عن الأيتام، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: One account says the question concerned taking charge of the orphans.
rows.anchor: فقيل: يسألونك عن القيام عليهم، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Another account says they asked about managing the orphans’ property and mixing with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عن التصرف في مالهم ومخالطتهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The question may concern managing the orphan’s personal affairs as well as property.
rows.anchor: عن تدبير أمره في نفسه وماله، عن القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to an orphan’s guardian: improving the orphans’ property without taking compensation is better and earns greater reward.
rows.anchor: المخاطب به ولي اليتيم، يعني إصلاح لأموالهم بغير عوض

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim understands reform as educating and correcting orphans as one would one’s own children.
rows.anchor: إصلاحهم بتأديبهم وتقويمهم مثل ما يفعله بولده، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation makes reform cover what benefits the orphan’s person and property.
rows.anchor: إصلاح لهم فيما يرجع إلى صلاح نفسه وماله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Mixing means sharing meals, expenses, and living arrangements; ‘they are your brothers’ grants permission to mix with them.
rows.anchor: تشاركوهم في مؤاكلتهم ونفقاتهم ومساكنتهم فإخوانكم أي فهم إخوانكم، وهذا إذن من الله تعالى في مخالطتهم، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says mixing can mean marrying female orphans and marrying from among them.
rows.anchor: تخالطوهم بأن تنكحوا منهن وتزوجوا منهم، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who corrupts orphans’ property and who improves it; he also knows intentions, including those seeking their property through marriage.
rows.anchor: يعلم ضمائر من أراد الإفساد والطمع في مالهم بالنكاح من المصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have made mixing with orphans difficult instead of granting this concession; another explanation says he could have destroyed people for their handling of orphan property.
rows.anchor: كما وسع عليكم بهذه الرخصة، ولو شاء شدد عليكم وضيق في مخالطتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Mighty’ means powerful and unable to be restrained; ‘wise’ means acting wisely despite power, with ‘knowing’ also reported as a gloss by Abū ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: عزيز قادر لا يجوز عليه المنع حكيم في أفعاله مع قدرته

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī glosses ‘wise’ here as ‘knowing.’
rows.anchor: وقيل: عليم، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is the opposite of security.
rows.anchor: الخوف: ضد الأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijāl is the plural of rājil, on the pattern of tājir/tujjār and other listed singular-plural pairs.
rows.anchor: والرجال جمع راجل، نحو تاجر وتجار وقائم وقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riding is mounting or being on something; rākib has the plural rukbān, like fāris/fursān.
rows.anchor: والركوب: العلو على الشيء يقال: راكب وركبان جمع راكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘On foot or riding’ and the following phrase are accusative circumstantial expressions with an omitted governing verb, ‘pray.’
rows.anchor: نصبا على الحال، والعامل فيه محذوف، وتقديره: فصلوا رجالا أو ركبانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding observance of prayer, God permits prayer in the presence of an enemy when fear prevents its full conditions and due performance.
rows.anchor: الرخصة حال العدو في الصلاة لما تقدم الأمر بالمحافظة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is explained as praying while walking on foot or riding on the backs of animals.
rows.anchor: قيل: مشاة على أرجلكم أو ركبانا على ظهور دوابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second gloss says to pray on foot or on the backs of animals, identifying this as the prayer of fear.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على أرجلكم أو ظهور دوابكم، وهو صلاة الخوف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan permits the prayer of fear to consist of one rakʿa.
rows.anchor: فقيل: يجوز ركعة، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: The Iraqi jurists say fear does not change the number of rakʿas: two while travelling and four while resident; Jishumi prefers this because one rakʿa is not a prayer and dawn prayer is not shortened.
rows.anchor: فأما أهل العراق فقالوا: لا يؤثر الخوف في عدد الركعات، ففي السفر ركعتان، وفي الحضر أربع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, like al-Shāfiʿī, allows prayer by gestures while walking or fighting, facing whatever direction one is going.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: يجوز، وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions do not allow prayer by gestures while walking and fighting.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When fear ends, the worshipper returns to the secure state of prayer.
rows.anchor: (فإذا أمنتم) زال الخوف

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد والأصم
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and al-Aṣamm understand remembering God as performing the complete prayer of a secure person, with all its pillars.
rows.anchor: قيل: صلوا صلاة الآمن بتمام أركانها (كما علمكم)، عن الحسن وابن زيد والأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the command as praising and extolling God for teaching people what they did not know of their religion.
rows.anchor: اذكروا الله بالحمد له والثناء عليه كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون من أمور دينكم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has the imperative lām in وليكتب with sukūn.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة (وليكتب) بسكون اللام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the lām in وليكتب with kasra.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن بكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is an imperative; when preceded by waw, fa, or thumma, most Arabs give it sukūn for ease, while others preserve its original kasra.
rows.anchor: وهذه لام الأمر، ولا يؤمر به غير الغائب

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the hamza of إن with kasra and فتذكر with indicative mood and shadda; he construes the phrase conditionally and as a new clause after the conditional fa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة إن تضل بكسر الألف فتذكر بالرفع والتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ḥamza’s reading, تضل is jussive in the conditional though its doubling obscures the form; فتذكر is indicative as the clause after the conditional fa begins anew.
rows.anchor: موضع تضل جزم بالجزاء إلا أنه لا يبين في التضعيف فتذكر رفع

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use fatḥ on أن and read فتذكر in connection with the preceding clause, with نصب either as the object of the verb or after an understood preposition أن.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بنصب الألف والراء على الاتصال بالكلام الأول

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم والكسائي وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn ʿĀmir read فتذكر with shadda and نصب; Ḥamza uses shadda and رفع, while Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr use a light form with نصب.
rows.anchor: التشديد والنصب نافع وعاصم والكسائي وابن عامر، وبالتشديد والرفع حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light and doubled forms are both Arabic usage, like dhakkara/adhkara and nazzala/anzala.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان نحو ذكر وأذكر، ونزل وأنزل

rows.speaker: عاصم والجحدري
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Jaḥdarī read تضل with passive morphology, ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥ on the ḍād.
rows.anchor: وعن عاصم والجحدري تضل بضم الياء وفتح الضاد على المجهول

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reads فتذاكر with an alif, as reciprocal discussion.
rows.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم فتذاكر بالألف من المذاكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can be parsed as a circumstantial clause, or as a predicate of an elided كان: ‘whether the debt is small or large.’
rows.anchor: قلنا: لوجهين: أحدهما: على الحال، والثاني: أن تجعله خبرا ل (كان)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding usury, God permits salam and debts; after commanding respite, he also commands fulfillment before documentation and witnesses.
rows.anchor: لما حرم تعالى الربا رخص في السلم والمداينات، فلما أمر بالإنظار أمر بالاستيفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi glosses the address as a call to affirm God and his messenger.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا صدقوا الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadayantum means that people deal with one another by lending or incurring a debt.
rows.anchor: إذا تداينتم أي داين بعضكم بعضا يعني أعطاه دينا بدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ‘debt’ is repeated because tadaayantum can mean either mutual repayment or dealings involving debt, so the repetition disambiguates the shared expression.
rows.anchor: ذكر الدين مع المداينة لوجهين: أحدهما: تخليص المشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition also reinforces the meaning in the mind, as in the emphatic Qur’anic phrases about the angels prostrating and birds flying with wings.
rows.anchor: الثاني: التأكيد على جهة تمكين المعنى في النفس

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says Bābil is a place name that does not decline.
rows.anchor: ببابل قيل: اسم بلد لا ينصرف، عن الكسائي

rows.speaker: الحسن وعائشة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀʾisha identify Bābil as Babylon in Iraq.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بابل العراق، عن الحسن، وعائشة

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī identify Bābil as Dinawand.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بابل ديناوند، عن الضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl derives the name Bābil from languages becoming confused and differing there.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: لأن ألسنتهم تبلبل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two mentioned as teaching are the angels.
rows.anchor: وما يعلمان من أحد يعني الملكين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: They warn that they are a test: magic is disclosed so people can avoid it and avoid unbelief through practicing it; they were sent to deter people and expose its falsehood.
rows.anchor: قيل: نحن امتحان واختبار نبين السحر ليجتنب ولا يكفر بعمل السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the two as a punishment for people who refuse to accept their advice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نحن عقوبة على من لا يقبل نصيحتنا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the angels neither received nor taught magic; they warned everyone they taught not to disbelieve, forbidding unbelief and magic.
rows.anchor: ينهيان عن الكفر والسحر، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the pair were non-Arabs; like a libertine warning others against his own error, they meant ‘we are misguided unbelievers, so do not disbelieve.’
rows.anchor: عن الحسن. ولا تكفر فيه ثلاثة أقوال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: One gloss forbids practicing magic; another forbids unbelief through learning magic; a third forbids either one, as separately stated by Abū ʿAlī and others.
rows.anchor: قيل: بعمل السحر، وقيل: لا تكفر بتعلم السحر

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads the warning as forbidding both magic and unbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من السحر والكفر، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأبو علي
rows.claim: Most commentators, including Abū ʿAlī, take ‘from the two’ to mean from the angels.
rows.anchor: من الملكين، عن أكثر المفسرين، وهو قول أبي علي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim understands them to learn magic and unbelief from the pair, in place of what the pair taught.
rows.anchor: من السحر والكفر، عن أبي مسلم، وتقديره: فيتعلمون مكان ما علمناه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says they learn from the devils and Hārūt and Mārūt.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الشياطين وهاروت وماروت، عن الأصم

words: مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they cause separation through slander and incitement that make spouses resent one another.
rows.anchor: قيل: بالنميمة والتضريب، فينغص كل واحد منهما إلى صاحبه، عن قتادة

words: مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ
rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says magic can lead to unbelief, which makes the wife forbidden and thus separates spouses.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مسلم وما هم يعني الذين يفرقون بين المرء وزوجه

words: وَمَا هُمْ بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who cause separation cannot harm anyone by magic except by God’s permission; the min is extra, yielding ‘they do not harm anyone.’
rows.anchor: يعني لا يلحقان ضررا بغيره إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: أبو علي والأصم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and al-Aṣamm explain God’s permission as his knowledge, citing the expression about being warned of war from God.
rows.anchor: قيل: بعلم الله تعالى، عن أبي علي والأصم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim notes the lexical distinction between idhn as permission and udhn as an ear, which he says can have the same sense like other paired forms.
rows.anchor: كشبه وشبه، ومثل ومثل، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God lets the magic harm some people but prevents it from harming others.
rows.anchor: قيل: بتخلية الله، قال: من شاء الله منعه من السحر

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān transmits a reading or gloss ‘except by God’s decree,’ understood here as knowledge.
rows.anchor: وروى سفيان: (إلا بقضاء الله) ويحمل على معنى العلم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī compares divine permission to ordinary causes such as diseases arising from poison or food.
rows.anchor: وهو كالأمراض التي تحصل عند سقي السم والأطعمة وغيره، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic harms its learners and does not benefit them because it leads to everlasting punishment.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يصيرون به إلى العذاب الدائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They knew’ refers to the Jews who cast God’s Book behind their backs.
rows.anchor: يعني اليهود الذين نبذوا كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: قتادة وزيد بن أسلم وجماعة
rows.claim: They ‘bought’ magic by choosing it instead of God’s religion; the pronoun refers to magic.
rows.anchor: استبدل السحر بدين الله، فالهاء في اشتراه كناية عن السحر، عن قتادة وابن زيد وجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says their purchase means they paid wages for magic.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يعطون الأجرة عليه، فذلك اشتراؤهم له، عن أبي علي

words: مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ
rows.speaker: مجاهد وسفيان والسدي
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Sufyān, and al-Suddī gloss the person’s share in the afterlife as a share of good.
rows.anchor: قيل: نصيب من الخير، عن مجاهد وسفيان والسدي

words: مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the phrase as meaning that the person has no religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما له دين، عن الحسن

words: مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss takes the phrase to mean that the person has no deliverance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من خلاص

rows.speaker: السدي وغيره
rows.claim: They sold their own share by choosing unbelief over faith.
rows.anchor: يعني ما باعوا به حظ أنفسهم، حيث اختاروا الكفر على الإيمان، عن السدي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pardon passage is said to have been particularized for many rather than all.
rows.anchor: خص به كثيرا دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: جماعة أهل العلم
rows.claim: The command to pardon is abrogated according to a group of scholars, showing that the pardon was temporary because it was tied to an endpoint.
rows.anchor: وتدل على جواز النسخ في القرآن؛ لأن قوله: فاعفوا منسوخ عند جماعة أهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdīm means the opposite of delaying.
rows.anchor: التقديم: نقيض التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can refer either to sight by the eye or to knowledge.
rows.anchor: وبصير: يستعمل في شيئين: الرؤية بالبصر، وفي العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is conditional and تجدوه is its apodosis, as in the verse about whatever mercy God opens for people.
rows.anchor: (ما) في قوله: وما تقدموا ما الجزاء، وجوابه: تجدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the Jews’ hostility, God commands Muslims to adhere to Islam and its laws, differing from them.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتمسك بدين الإسلام وشرائعه مخالفة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish prayer means to keep it up continually.
rows.anchor: وأقيموا الصلاة أي أديموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give zakat means give it to the poor; zakat is the share God obligates the poor to receive from the wealth of the rich.
rows.anchor: وآتوا الزكاة أي أعطوها الفقراء، والزكاة ما أوجب الله تعالى للفقراء في مال الأغنياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Good’ sent ahead is explained as righteous action, its reward, or wealth.
rows.anchor: يعني من عمل صالح، وقيل: من ثواب، وقيل: من مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is sent ahead is found with God as reward already prepared, as recompense owed by God, or as a preserved and recorded deed for which he repays the servant.
rows.anchor: تجدوا ثوابه معدا عند الله، وقيل: تجدوه مستحقا على الله أن يكافئه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase must refer to human deeds: exhortation attaches to deeds, and a servant’s acts cannot be restored as such.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يريد غير أفعالهم؛ لأن الترغيب لا يقع بوجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ‘with Us’ can refer to trusts rather than obligations, God’s certain provision of recompense makes it like returning a deposit.
rows.anchor: يوفر الجزاء لا محالة كان كرد الوديعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows people’s deeds and repays them according to what they deserve, so they should act knowing nothing is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: أي عليم بأفعالكم يجازيكم بما تستحقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates worship through prayer and zakat and that they are two pillars, which is why they are singled out.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على التعبد بالصلاة والزكاة، وأنهما من الأركان؛ لذلك خصهما بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is due only on specified grazing camels, cattle, and sheep when they reach a full taxable minimum and a complete year passes; it is not due on working or stall-fed animals.
rows.anchor: في مال مخصوص، وهو السوائم من الإبل والبقر والغنم، إذا كان نصابا كاملا، وحال عليه حول كامل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa includes property acquired during the year with the original taxable property.
rows.anchor: ويضم المستفاد في أثناء الحول إلى الأصل عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī does not add property acquired during the year to the original taxable property.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا يضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specified term is a stated and known time.
rows.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى وقت مسمى، وقيل: نزلت الآية خاصة في السلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed specifically about salam sales.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت الآية خاصة في السلم، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: المفسرون والفقهاء
rows.claim: The exegetes and jurists apply the verse to every debt and sale price, whether the sold item is delivered now or later.
rows.anchor: في كل دين وثمن بمبيع مسلم وغيره، وعليه المفسرون والفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mussammā means that the term is stated and known.
rows.anchor: مسمى أي مذكور معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing down the debt prevents later forgetfulness or denial.
rows.anchor: فاكتبوه أي اكتبوا الدين؛ لئلا يقع فيه نسيان أو جحود

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والحسن
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and al-Ḥasan, with most scholars, treat writing the debt as recommended.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هو ندب، عن أبي سعيد الخدري والحسن وعليه الأكثر

rows.speaker: الربيع وكعب
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and Kaʿb regard writing the debt as obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فرض، عن الربيع وكعب

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that writing, witnessing, and pledging were once obligatory and were abrogated by the following verse’s allowance when parties trust each other; Jishumi prefers the view that writing is recommended as a means of securing rights.
rows.anchor: كانت الكتابة والإشهاد والرهن واجبا فنسخ بقوله تعالى: فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا الآية، عن الشعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scribe records the debt or sale between the parties with fairness, neither adding nor subtracting nor harming either without their knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني وليكتب كتاب المداينة أو البيع بين المتعاقدين كاتب بالعدل أي بالحق والإنصاف

rows.speaker: الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and other exegetes say writing is a communal obligation, like jihad; Jishumi says this is the view followed in practice.
rows.anchor: قيل: الكتابة واجبة على الكفاية كالجهاد ونحوه، عن الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the duty applies to the scribe when he is free to write.
rows.anchor: وقيل: واجب على الكاتب في حال فراغه، عن السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء والربيع
rows.claim: Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Rabīʿ say writing is obligatory when the scribe is asked.
rows.anchor: وقيل: واجب إذا أمر، عن مجاهد وعطاء والربيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the command that a scribe not refuse was abrogated by the instruction not to harm a scribe or witness; the adopted practice is the first view, communal obligation.
rows.anchor: قيل: نسختها: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد والعمل على القول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is emphasized because scribes were few in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: وكانت الكتبة فيهم قلة على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor should dictate by acknowledging in his own words what he owes, so the amount due is known.
rows.anchor: يعني المطلوب المديون يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must avoid disobeying God’s command and must not reduce any part of the debt.
rows.anchor: أي يتقي مخالفة أمره ولا يبخس منه شيئا لا ينقص من الحق شيئا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses safīh as someone ignorant about dictation.
rows.anchor: قيل: جاهلا بالإملاء، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk gloss safīh as a young child.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طفلا صغيرا عن السدي والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses safīh as incapable or foolish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عاجزا أحمق، عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak is explained as sick or senile with age; unable to dictate includes muteness, foreign speech, or similar inability.
rows.anchor: قيل: مريضا، وقيل: شيخا خرفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو، أي لا يقدر على الإملاء لخرس أو عجمة

words: سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi says the three categories should be understood as distinct to avoid repetition: mentally disabled, young, and unable to dictate, with comparable cases included under each.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أن يحمل على ثلاث صفات لكيلا يؤدي إلى التكرار

words: سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī’s preferred mapping is a spendthrift for safīh, an adolescent child for weak, and an insane person as unable to dictate; each label may include equivalents.
rows.anchor: السفيه: المبذر، والضعيف: الصبي المراهق، ومن لا يستطيع أن يمل المجنون عن القاضي

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd say the guardian of the incompetent person dictates what that person owes, acting in his place.
rows.anchor: ولي السفيه يملي ما على السفيه، فيقوم مقامه، عن الضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, and Muqātil identify the guardian as the creditor, who knows the debt and dictates it fairly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولي الحق، عن ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل؛ لأنه أعلم بدينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction is to seek witnesses and have them testify to the written record; two men suffice generally, except that adultery requires four.
rows.anchor: يعني اطلبوا الشهود وأشهدوا على المكتوب، شهيدين يعني رجلين

rows.speaker: مجاهد وجماعة من الفقهاء
rows.claim: Mujāhid and many jurists restrict the male witnesses to free, adult Muslims, excluding non-Muslims, slaves, and children.
rows.anchor: قيل: من الأحرار البالغين المسلمين دون الكفار والعبيد والصبيان، عن مجاهد وجماعة من الفقهاء

rows.speaker: شريح وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Shurayḥ and Ibn Sīrīn permit testimony by slaves.
rows.anchor: وأجاز شريح وابن سيرين شهادة العبيد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik permits children’s testimony in cases of assault injuries.
rows.anchor: وأجاز مالك شهادة الصبيان في الجراح

rows.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي والشافعي
rows.claim: Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, and al-Shāfiʿī restrict the male-and-two-women arrangement to financial matters.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذا في الأموال خاصة، عن مالك والأوزاعي والشافعي

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: Iraqi jurists apply it to all matters except fixed criminal penalties and retaliation.
rows.anchor: الحدود والقصاص، وهو قول أهل العراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptable witnesses are upright in religion, trustworthy, and competent; another gloss requires that no suspicion or accusation attach to them.
rows.anchor: يعني من كان مرضيا في دينه وأمانته وكفايته وهو العدل

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm defines an acceptable witness as someone who has not shown cause for suspicion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العدل المرضي من لم يظهر منه ريبة، عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī describes a trustworthy witness as one not accused in matters of appetite or sexual conduct.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من لم يطعن عليه في بطن ولا فرج، عن الشعبي

rows.speaker: الربيع والسدي والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ, al-Suddī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Zayd, and most exegetes take ‘go astray’ as forget, so one woman reminds the other of the testimony.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو من الذكر أي تذكرها الشهادة، عن الربيع والسدي والضحاك وابن زيد وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna instead understands the reminder as making one woman like a male witness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الذكر أي تجعلها كذكر من الرجال، عن سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi rejects the ‘make her like a man’ gloss because the preceding condition that one may err indicates that reminder means recalling the testimony.
rows.anchor: وهذا يبعد لأنه تقدم قوله: (تضل) فدل أن المراد به الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl originally means destruction.
rows.anchor: الويل: أصله الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasb is an act that obtains benefit or wards off harm; its root sense is seeking provision and obtaining benefit.
rows.anchor: والكسب: فعل يجتلب به نفعا، أو يدفع به ضررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawayl is nominative as an initial subject; Arabic also permits an accusative construction, though it is not read.
rows.anchor: (فويل) رفع لأنه مبتدأ به، ويجوز في العربية النصب، ولا يقرأ به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والأصم وأبو علي وأبو مسلم وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Aṣamm, Abū ʿAlī, Abū Muslim, and others say it concerns Jewish scholars who altered scripture for ordinary people, fearing loss of status and changing the Prophet’s description; Jishumi prefers this as continuous with the context.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أحبار اليهود، وعلمائهم الذين حرفوا الكتاب على العوام، عن ابن عباس والأصم وأبي علي وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abū Mālik reports that the verse concerns a scribe who altered what he dictated for the Prophet, then apostatized and died; the earth expelled his body. Jishumi rejects this as less fitting because the passage continues its discussion of Jews.
rows.anchor: ثم ارتد ومات، فلفظته الأرض، عن أبي مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi distinguishes Jews who knowingly distort scripture, those unable to read or understand who follow scholars by conjecture, and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: صنف اليهود فجعل بعضهم محرفين مع العلم، وبعضهم غير عارفين بالقراءة والمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others gloss wayl as punishment.
rows.anchor: قيل: الويل: العذاب عن ابن عباس وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes wayl as censure; it may also express grief and lament, as in ‘Oh woe to us, what is this book?’
rows.anchor: وقيل: الويل: تقبيح، ومنه قوله تعالى: (ولكم الويل)

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses wayl as disgrace.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الويل: الخزي، عن الفراء

rows.speaker: الخدري
rows.claim: Al-Khudrī transmits from the Prophet that wayl is a valley in Hell into which an unbeliever falls for forty years before reaching its bottom.
rows.anchor: واد في جهنم يهوي فيه الكافر أربعين خريفا قبل أن يبلغ قعره، رواه الخدري عن النبي

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān transmits from the Prophet that wayl is a mountain in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جبل في النار، عن عثمان يرويه عن النبي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib also says wayl is a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: واد في جهنم، عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm and others say wayl is a word uttered by anyone distressed and falling into ruin.
rows.anchor: ويل كلمة يقولها كل مكروب إذا وقع في هلكة، عن الأصم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred explanation is that the writers altered the Prophet’s description in their scripture; other reports say they changed his described complexion and stature or changed lawful and forbidden rulings.
rows.anchor: قيل: حرفوا صفة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says they changed his description from dark and medium-statured to fair and elderly; another says they altered lawful and forbidden rulings.
rows.anchor: كان صفته أسمر ربعة، فكتبوا آدم كهل، وقيل: حرفوا الحلال والحرام

words: وَلَا يَأْبَ الشُّهَدَاءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا
rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء والشعبي والسدي وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Shaʿbī, al-Suddī, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr take the call as one to give testimony in court; the Qāḍī chooses this view.
rows.anchor: لإقامتها، عن مجاهد وعطاء والشعبي والسدي وسعيد بن جبير، وهو الذي اختاره القاضي

words: وَلَا يَأْبَ الشُّهَدَاءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan understand the call to cover both bearing and giving testimony.
rows.anchor: لإثباتها وإقامتها، عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reject interpreting the call as bearing testimony because the people have not yet become witnesses; Jishumi answers that the command to seek two witnesses makes them witnesses.
rows.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم حمل الآية على التحمل؛ لأنهم ليسوا بشهداء، وهذا الاحتجاج يبطل بقوله: واستشهدوا شهيدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse concerns bearing testimony, that duty is variously described as communal obligation, recommendation, or permission; if giving testimony, it is communal when others can do it and individual when no substitute exists.
rows.anchor: فقيل: واجب على الكفاية، وقيل: هو أمر ندب، وقيل: هو إباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not tire of documenting the debt, whether small or large, and continue through its due date; another view refers to the witness’s term.
rows.anchor: لا تملوا أن تكتبوه صغيرا كان الحق أو كبيرا قليلا كان المال أو كبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term is explained as the due date of the debt or, alternatively, the witness’s term.
rows.anchor: إلى أجله يعني محل الدين والحق، وقيل: إلى أجل الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writing is more just before God because he commanded it, and obeying his command is more just than leaving it; it is also sounder for testimony and nearer to removing doubt.
rows.anchor: واتباع أمره أعدل من تركه وأقوم للشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is an immediate cash sale, hand to hand, with no deferred term; documenting it is not required and causes no harm or financial burden.
rows.anchor: تجارة حاضرة يدا بيد نقدا غير نسيئة ولا فيه أجل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk considers witnessing a sale obligatory.
rows.anchor: قيل: الإشهاد فرض عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن والشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Shāfiʿī regard witnessing sales as recommended, which Jishumi says is the jurists’ position.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ندب، عن الحسن والشافعي، وهو قول الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the active reading, the underlying form is yudārir with kasra; the writer and witness are the agents.
rows.anchor: أصله ولا يضارر، بكسر الراء، والفاعل الكاتب والشهيد

rows.speaker: عطاء وطاووس والحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: The writer must not be harmed by being forbidden to write or made to add or subtract from what was dictated; the witness must not be made to refuse or testify to what he does not know.
rows.anchor: لا يضار كاتب بألا يكتب، أو يكتب ما لم يملل بزيادة أو نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the passive reading, the writer and witness are the objects of harm.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على الفعل المجهول والكاتب والشهيد مفعولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading means not to burden a writer or witness when called for an important need; another person should be summoned if possible.
rows.anchor: يعني لا يضارر بفتح الراء: الكاتب والشاهد إذا دعوا، وهما على حاجة مهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden conduct is understood as harming the writer and witness or doing what was prohibited and disobeying what was commanded; it is departure from God’s obedience.
rows.anchor: قيل: ما نهيتكم عنه من الضرار، وقيل: إن تفعلوا ما نهيتكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā here means avoiding disobedience and sin, or safeguarding trusts by discharging them.
rows.anchor: يعني اتقوا مخالفة أمره والفسوق، وقيل: اتقوا في الأمانات ألا تؤدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches people what benefits them in religious and worldly affairs, which they did not know.
rows.anchor: ما فيه صلاحكم في أمر دينكم ودنياكم ما لم تعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge is glossed as universal, knowledge of people’s deeds and recompense, or knowledge of their interests that informs his commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو عام أي عالم بجميع الأشياء لا يخفى عليه شيء

rows.speaker: عروة عن عائشة
rows.claim: ʿUrwa reports from ʿĀʾisha that the verse concerned the Anṣār, who had venerated Manāt before Islam and avoided saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwa; after becoming Muslim they asked the Prophet whether they could perform it, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى عروة عن عائشة أنها نزلت في الأنصار، وأنهم كانوا قبل الإسلام يهلون لمناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining that God tests servants with commands, prohibitions, and afflictions according to their interests, Jishumi presents pilgrimage and saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwa as part of that testing and as divine rites.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى أنه يبتلي عباده بالأوامر والنواهي مرة، والمصائب أخرى على حسب مصالحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view sees no ellipsis: Ṣafā and Marwa are God’s signs and landmarks, the places of ritual and worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا حذف فيه، والمراد إن الصفا والمروة من أعلامه وآياته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses God’s rites as the pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: من المناسك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses God’s rites as his religion.
rows.anchor: من دين الله، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they are signs by which God made people know that the place is for worship.
rows.anchor: من أعلامه التي عرف عباده بأنه موضع عبادة، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrimage means intending the House through its prescribed actions; ʿumra is performing its prescribed rites and is described as an increase in the rites.
rows.anchor: أي قصده بالأفعال المشروعة أو اعتمر أي أتى بالعمرة، وهي الزيادة بالمناسك المشروعة

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
rows.speaker: أبو علي وجماعة
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and others posit an omitted ‘not’ in ‘there is no blame,’ as in the verses saying God clarifies lest people go astray and lest they say something on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أي لا حرج عليه أن يطوف بهما فحذف (لا) كقوله: (يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا)

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī rejects the proposed deleted ‘not’ because it is unnecessary; ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says deletion is valid only when context signals it.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي: وهذا لا يصح؛ لأنه يستغنى عن هذه الزيادة

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means there is no sin in performing the saʿy; removing sin implies the act is good, although the wording of no blame ordinarily conveys permission.
rows.anchor: معناه لا إثم عليه في الطواف بينهما، ورفع الإثم يدل على أن ذلك الفعل حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwa is worship but differ over whether it is obligatory or recommended, so the occasion is needed to explain the wording as permission.
rows.anchor: لكن العلماء اتفقوا أن الطواف بينهما عبادة، وإن اختلفوا أنه واجب أو ندب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verse answers the Anṣār, who thought saʿy unlawful; apart from that occasion, the verse would indicate that saʿy is obligatory.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هو جواب لقولهم، إنه لا يحل، وإلا فهو واجب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī take voluntary good as extra circumambulation around the House after the obligatory rites.
rows.anchor: قيل: فزاد في الطواف حول البيت بعد الواجب، عن ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو علي
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Abū ʿAlī understand it as voluntarily performing saʿy while believing it to be sunnah rather than obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من تطوع بالطواف بالصفا والمروة وعنده أنه سنة وليس بواجب، عن مجاهد وأبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes tatawwaʿ as performing ʿumra, with pilgrimage obligatory and ʿumra voluntary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تطوع بمعنى اعتمر فالحج فريضة والعمرة تطوع، عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says it means voluntarily performing pilgrimage or ʿumra after completing the obligatory one; both can be obligatory or voluntary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فمن تطوع بالحج والعمرة بعد قضاء الواجب، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes voluntary good broadly as the whole religion and all kinds of obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تطوع خيرا يعني الدين كله وأنواع الطاعات، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards those who do good with the best reward and knows what they deserve.
rows.anchor: يعني يجازي من أحسن بالحسنى والثواب، وهو عليم بقدر ما استحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ‘appreciative’ means God accepts the deed, and ‘knowing’ refers to the intention.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شاكر يقبله منه، عليم بما نوى، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say God knows the measure of the reward and does not shortchange anyone, or knows all the servants’ circumstances and recompenses them for their acts.
rows.anchor: عليم بقدر الجزاء فلا يبخس حقه، وقيل: عليم بجميع أحوال العباد
